scope: Read-only cross-check of event review core, build-host bridges, existing source-navigation lifecycle, new PROJECT_EVENTS documentation and focused tests.
result: No actionable identity, lifecycle or overclaim issue found in the reviewed changes.
checks: Core validates the complete observation before exposing a branded frozen model; p10 joins only explicit eventSequence/subscriptionId pairs, after existing validation of full recipient origins, callback uniqueness, pending queue head and retired event subscriptions.

Protocols 3–9 preserve event and delivery evidence with unavailable-protocol association status. Initial, direct and completion entries are excluded from event joins; not-recorded is not interpreted as a rejected condition.

Host forwards event and controller selection through explicit ports and consumes isCurrent. Both components receive the same validated run identity; independent list filters do not change the selected review.

Source reads retain frozen origin/source metadata, check initial busy admission, then use continuation ownership and the shared navigation epoch. Dirty drafts, creation, selection, visits, runs, source identity and dialog closing revoke outdated reads; own loading does not revoke a valid read.

New documentation accurately distinguishes pending callbacks, handled-without-entry, skipped subscriptions, explicit association and absent old-protocol evidence. It does not claim guard-evaluation traces, transition selection, playback completion, installed-device validation or a protocol upgrade in this increment.

Focused tests cover forged/partial models, accessor rejection, old protocols, repeated names and visits, shared scripts, exact joins, pending/handled changes, source tickets, filter independence, stale detached controls and host selection bridges.
